key_insight: VULCAN combines Hamiltonian-gradient-free ansatz growth, circuit compression, and perturbative correction to reduce the measurement cost of quantum chemistry calculations.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets measurement overhead, circuit depth, and qubit requirements, offering a resource-efficient pathway toward larger quantum chemistry simulations.
method: Grow full operator layers using Variational Double Bracket Flow and a linearly scaling pool, avoiding Hamiltonian-gradient measurements for operator selection.
Compress circuits through state-overlap measurements and reduce qubit requirements via dominant-determinant subspace projection.
Apply GPU-accelerated stochastic Epstein–Nesbet perturbation theory (ENPT2) to recover residual correlation and enable early termination.
evidence_signal: Emulation up to 32 logical qubits reports chemical accuracy at 5–20% of batched ADAPT-VQE's measurement cost for hydrogen chains, BeH2, and H2O; one VULCAN layer plus ENPT2 also reaches chemical accuracy for 32-qubit C3H6.
watch_item: Results rely on emulation; robustness to hardware noise and the total cost of compression and classical ENPT2 post-processing remain implementation concerns.
paper_title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
